```{r workflow-options, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = FALSE)
```

These recipes use the [GitHub development build](https://github.com/xec-cm/biocroxytest/tree/devel).
Start with [your first test](biocroxytest.html) and
[cases in memory and HDF5](named-cases.html) if you have not generated tests
yet. The first two recipes below run the same sample-alignment cases;
the later sections are configuration reference for your own package.

## Prepare the example package

Install SummarizedExperiment, HDF5Array and testthat 3.3.0 or newer, as in
the named-cases tutorial. This makes a fresh copy of the bundled package
and replaces its first test with the two named cases. All paths point to
the temporary copy, so the installed example stays unchanged.

```{r prepare-workflows, message=FALSE}
template <- system.file("examples", "samplealignment", package = "biocroxytest", mustWork = TRUE)
pkg <- tempfile("samplealignment-")
fs::dir_copy(template, pkg)
declaration <- system.file("examples", "steps", "named-cases.R", package = "biocroxytest", mustWork = TRUE)
file.copy(declaration, file.path(pkg, "R", "align-samples.R"), overwrite = TRUE)
withr::with_dir(pkg, biocroxytest::use_longtests())
roxygen2::roxygenise(pkg)
```

## Require particular cases in CI

A successful suite can contain skipped tests. If a CI job exists to test
HDF5, explicitly require the HDF5 case to complete. Choose the required
IDs yourself: deriving them from the report would overlook a case that
was accidentally removed.

```{r require-cases}
required <- c("sample-alignment/memory", "sample-alignment/hdf5")
evidence <- biocroxytest::run_test_plan(pkg, ids = required, seed = 42L, timeout = 60)
biocroxytest::check_test_plan(evidence, required)
evidence$cases[c("id", "status", "warnings")]
```

Both rows should show `completed` and zero warnings. `check_test_plan()`
returns silently when that policy is met; it errors otherwise. A required
ID absent from the declarations is rejected by `run_test_plan()` itself.
These errors give a nonzero exit status when left uncaught in `Rscript`.

In your CI checkout, create `tools/` if needed, save the following as
`tools/check-cases.R`, and run `Rscript --vanilla tools/check-cases.R`
**from the package root**, after installing the package's development
and test dependencies. Replace the IDs with the cases that this job
must exercise.

```{r ci-script, eval=FALSE}
required <- c("sample-alignment/memory", "sample-alignment/hdf5")
evidence <- biocroxytest::run_test_plan(ids = required, seed = 42L, timeout = 60)
biocroxytest::check_test_plan(evidence, required)
```

For example, a dependency-specific job should not accept a case that
called `skip_if_not_installed()`. A pilot using a DESeq2 contrast test in
[dar at `27c4da2`](https://github.com/MicrobialGenomics-IrsicaixaOrg/dar/blob/27c4da2/tests/testthat/test-model-adapters.R)
passed with DESeq2 present and rejected a deliberate skip that simulated
its absence.

Use `allow_warnings = TRUE` only when your policy permits completed cases
with recorded warnings. Warnings asserted with `expect_warning()` are
handled by the test and do not count. Older reports without warning
counts need a fresh run to satisfy the default policy.

### Interpret an execution report

Each named case runs in a fresh R session and temporary package copy.
The report records its duration, diagnostics, fixture checks, source
fingerprint and observed R environment.

| Status | Meaning | Meets the required-case policy? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `completed` | Reached the end with a passing expectation and no skips | Yes, with zero recorded warnings by default |
| `failed` | A test expectation or test code failed | No |
| `skipped` | The case skipped before recording a pass | No |
| `incomplete` | Execution did not establish completion | No |
| `missing` | A generated test or its result was absent | No |

Examples of `incomplete` include stale generated code, an unavailable
required fixture, an early return, a partial skip and a timeout. The
`detail` column explains the reason. `timeout` limits each isolated
process in seconds, including package loading and suite hooks. Copying
inputs and preparing fixtures happen before that limit starts. After a
timeout, the plan continues with the remaining cases.

Keep the normal full-suite checks too: running cases individually does
not exercise custom suite runners or dependencies between tests in one
session.

## Save and compare reports

The following example makes **two runs on this machine**, with the same
source, fixtures, seed and IDs. It demonstrates the comparison procedure;
it is not evidence of portability across platforms. Reports are saved
outside the package tree so that saving them does not change the source
fingerprint.

```{r save-reports}
reports <- tempfile("case-reports-")
dir.create(reports)
saveRDS(evidence, file.path(reports, "left.rds"))
second <- biocroxytest::run_test_plan(pkg, ids = required, seed = 42L, timeout = 60)
biocroxytest::check_test_plan(second, required)
saveRDS(second, file.path(reports, "right.rds"))
```

For a real comparison, run the same command in each CI environment and
download each saved report. Use those files in place of `left.rds` and
`right.rds` below. Match the cases to an independently chosen list of
expected IDs, rather than only comparing IDs present in both reports.

```{r compare-reports}
left <- readRDS(file.path(reports, "left.rds"))
right <- readRDS(file.path(reports, "right.rds"))
expected <- c("sample-alignment/memory", "sample-alignment/hdf5")

summarize_run <- function(report) {
  cases <- report$cases[match(expected, report$cases$id), ]
  warnings <- cases$warnings
  if (is.null(warnings)) warnings <- rep(NA_integer_, length(expected))
  context <- function(field) {
    vapply(expected, function(id) {
      value <- report$environments[[id]][[field]]
      if (is.null(value)) NA_character_ else value
    }, character(1))
  }
  data.frame(
    id = expected, status = cases$status, warnings = warnings,
    r_version = context("r_version"), platform = context("platform")
  )
}

comparison <- merge(summarize_run(left), summarize_run(right),
                    by = "id", suffixes = c(".left", ".right"), all = TRUE)
comparison[c("id", "status.left", "status.right", "warnings.left", "warnings.right")]
```

Both cases should be `completed` in both runs. An `NA` status means an
expected ID has no row in that report, including when it is absent from
both. The status `missing` means the report contains the ID but its test
or result was missing. An `NA` warning count can also identify an older
report that did not record warnings.

Inspect the context before interpreting differences:

```{r compare-context}
comparison[c("id", "r_version.left", "r_version.right", "platform.left", "platform.right")]
c(left = left$revision, right = right$revision)
```

Record the source commit and fixture checksums with each CI job. The
revision hash includes R's serialization header, so identical inputs can
produce different hashes under different R versions. For a case ID, use
`report$environments[[id]]$packages` to inspect loaded package versions
and `report$fixtures[[id]]` for declared fixture checks. An installed or
loaded dependency alone does not establish which backend a test used;
assert its actual backing class in the test, as in the HDF5 tutorial.

## Review changes to the declared cases

A plan comparison answers a different question from comparing run reports:
what changed in the declarations? Here we move the HDF5 case into the ordinary
suite while keeping its ID and assertions.

```{r compare-plans}
before <- biocroxytest::test_case_plan(pkg)
source_file <- file.path(pkg, "R", "align-samples.R")
original <- readLines(source_file)
moved <- sub('hdf5 = list(suite = "longtests"', 'hdf5 = list(suite = "tests"',
              original, fixed = TRUE)
writeLines(moved, source_file)
changes <- biocroxytest::compare_test_plans(before, biocroxytest::test_case_plan(pkg))
changes[c("id", "status", "before_suite", "after_suite")]
```

The result should identify `sample-alignment/hdf5` as `moved`, from
`longtests` to `tests`. The comparison does not run tests. It also reports
added, removed and changed cases; a renamed ID appears as a removal and
an addition. Restore the original source for the remaining recipes:

```{r restore-plan}
stopifnot(identical(changes$id, "sample-alignment/hdf5"),
          identical(changes$status, "moved"))
writeLines(original, source_file)
```

If you keep a declaration change, regenerate its tests before execution.

## Check that generated files are current

Commit generated tests with their source declarations. In CI, run this
command from the package root after installing development dependencies:

```sh
Rscript --vanilla -e 'biocroxytest::check_generated_tests()'
```

The check regenerates tests in a temporary copy and fails if owned
outputs are missing, changed or obsolete. It leaves your checkout in
place. To resolve a failure, run `roxygen2::roxygenise()` locally, inspect
the generated diff, and commit the intended changes. Use
`biocroxytest::generated_test_inventory()` to list files, source paths
and suites. This checks generation; run the tests themselves as well.

## Include extra files in isolated runs

Most packages need no additional configuration. The copy used by named
case execution and generated-file checks contains the usual package
inputs, both test suites, their helpers and local fixtures. The revision
fingerprint covers the copied paths and contents.

If your tests or roclet read files from another directory, add each path
to `DESCRIPTION`. For example, if `dev/example-code.R` and
`reference-data/` exist in your package:

```text
Config/biocroxytest/inputs: dev/example-code.R
    reference-data
```

Paths must be relative to the package root and refer to ordinary files
or directories. This can retain build-excluded development inputs;
excluded R source files still stay excluded.

The default manifest includes `DESCRIPTION`, `NAMESPACE`, `.BBSoptions`,
`.Rbuildignore`, `.Rinstignore`, license and build scripts, and the
standard directories `R`, `src`, `data`, `inst`, `man`, `vignettes`,
`demo`, `po`, `tools` and `exec`. It also retains roxygen templates in
`man-roxygen`, tooling in `man/roxygen`, and both test suites in full.
Git metadata and standard editor/native build artifacts are omitted.
Build-ignore patterns are matched without regard to case.

Remove newly excluded R files from any `Collate` fields before checking
generated tests or installing the package. Direct calls to
`roxygen2::roxygenise()` use its configured loader, which can load ignored
R files before the roclet selects sources. Older replay records retain
their original source-selection and full-checkout fingerprint rules.

## Test values from documented examples

`@testexamples` lets the ordinary suite check values produced by a
topic's `@examples`. In the example package, this complete block can
replace `R/align-samples.R`; it replaces that file's named cases too.
Regenerate tests and run the ordinary suite after the edit.

```{r documented-examples, eval=FALSE}
#' Select samples in the requested order
#'
#' @param x A SummarizedExperiment.
#' @param samples Sample names in the requested order.
#' @return A SummarizedExperiment with the selected samples.
#' @export
#' @examples
#' selected <- align_samples(example_experiment(), c("s3", "s1"))
#' @testexamples
#' expect_identical(colnames(selected), c("s3", "s1"))
#' expect_identical(selected$condition, c("treated", "control"))
align_samples <- function(x, samples) x[, samples]
```

The generated ordinary test runs direct examples before their assertions.
It omits `\dontrun{}` and executes `\dontshow{}` and `\donttest{}`.
An `@examplesIf` condition runs in sequence and skips the test if false.
Rd platform directives are resolved during generation. Inherited
examples, templates and Rd `\Sexpr{}` expressions are outside this
workflow.

## Migrate from roxytest

Start in a disposable copy of your package with its current tests passing.
In the `Roxygen` field of `DESCRIPTION`, replace
`roxytest::testthat_roclet` and any `biocroxytest::longtests_roclet` with
`biocroxytest::tests_roclet`, retaining your other roclets. Use one test
generator per destination.

Regenerate with the default `clean = FALSE`, inspect the diff, and run
both configured suites. Ordinary roxytest filename prefixes are retained
and generated ownership headers are updated. For shared `@rdname`
topics, tags follow their source files. Review snapshot paths and test
descriptions if a test moves. Keep your existing helpers, custom runners
and manual tests.

## Remove the temporary example

When you have finished inspecting the reports, remove only the paths
created by this page:

```{r cleanup-workflows}
if (isNamespaceLoaded("samplealignment")) pkgload::unload("samplealignment")
unlink(c(pkg, reports), recursive = TRUE)
```

For a failing case, continue with [failure replay](replay-walkthrough.html).
